signal_to_noise.rationale: No tests means no noise, but also no signal; per the anchor this is a neutral 3.

findings.issue: The app ships zero tests: no test script, no runner dependency, no spec files anywhere in app/.
findings.suggestion: Add Vitest + @testing-library/react (TanStack's recommended stack) with a `test` script, and start with the pure helpers and the cache layer, which need no DOM at all.

findings.issue: The TTL cache's failure eviction (line 24-26) is load-bearing but untested; a refactor that drops it caches rejected promises for 60s, turning one transient API error into a minute of hard failures.
findings.suggestion: Unit test `memo` with fake timers: TTL expiry, failure eviction, concurrent callers sharing one promise.

findings.issue: Search input, debounced URL sync (lastPushed ref) and filter/pagination interact through three pieces of state with no coverage; line 75 compares untrimmed local query to trimmed URL q, silently forcing page 1 when the user types a trailing space, and back/forward navigation is untested.
findings.suggestion: Add component tests for: typing updates results then URL; browser back restores input state; ?page out of range clamps; whitespace-only q is omitted from the URL.

findings.issue: getPokemonById(species.id) is not wrapped in orNull, so a species whose default Pokémon is missing throws the internal NotFoundError past the notFound() flow, rendering the framework error boundary instead of the spec's Not-found page.
findings.suggestion: Wrap in orNull and throw notFound() when either lookup fails; add a test for the species-without-default-Pokémon case.

findings.issue: The home index is derived by cross-joining type and generation lists; species missing from those lists silently get types:[] / generation:null and vanish from the filters — exactly the failure mode a data-layer refactor would introduce.
findings.suggestion: Unit test speciesIndex against a small fixture with a two-type species, a typeless species, and a generation-less species, asserting the degradation is at least explicit.

findings.issue: The sort comparator's nulls-last-in-both-directions logic and stable index tie-break (line 58) are subtle and untested; the acceptance suite only exercises one column on one Pokémon.
findings.suggestion: Extract the comparator or test the component with rows containing null power/accuracy, asserting ascending and descending order and aria-sort state.

findings.issue: toCards (alternate-form exclusion via id > 10000, dedupe by species id, fallback name when the species map is stale) is untested; the stale-TTL fallback at line 105 is a genuine edge the acceptance suite only partially covers.
findings.suggestion: Unit test with refs including IDs above 10000, duplicate species refs, and an ID absent from the species map.

findings.issue: Non-404 API failures (500s, connection refused) propagate unhandled; no route defines an errorComponent, so an API outage yields the framework default error page without the required layout or title.
findings.suggestion: Add an errorComponent (at least on the root) and a test that an API 500 renders something reasonable rather than an unhandled rejection.

findings.issue: Default game selection relies on sorting by version-group order with a name tie-break and a MAX_SAFE_INTEGER fallback; the `.at(-1)` highest-order pick is easy to invert in a refactor.
findings.suggestion: Unit test the game-ordering logic with a fixture of version groups with known and missing orders.

findings.issue: humanize, collapse, latestEnglish (pokeapi.ts:73-75) and display are pure and used site-wide (latestEnglish must take the last English entry, collapse must handle \f), yet have no tests.
findings.suggestion: A single spec file covering humanize ('mr-mime' → 'Mr Mime', 'ho-oh' → 'Ho Oh'), collapse of \n\f runs, and latestEnglish taking the last entry would be ~15 minutes of work with high regression value.

summary: The app contains no tests of its own — no runner, no script, no spec files — so every behaviour beyond the harness's acceptance suite is unguarded. That unguarded surface is large and genuinely risky: a TTL cache whose failure eviction is load-bearing, a three-way search/URL/debounce state machine with a trailing-space page-reset quirk, data derivation that silently drops type/generation for edge data, and one real latent bug (getPokemonById without orNull bypasses the not-found flow). Given Vitest is TanStack's recommended runner and much of this logic is pure and cheaply testable, this is the app's biggest gap as a long-term codebase.
